Quality, Audit & Patient Safety

Quality, patient safety and risk management — pillars of quality care, accreditation, safety programmes and stress.

🎯 After this chapter you can

  • Describe the pillars of quality care
  • Explain accreditation and standards
  • Describe patient safety programmes
  • Apply risk management and stress reduction

In simple words

Quality care means doing the right thing, at the right time, in the right way, and getting a safe outcome for every patient.

Pillars of quality

Pillar Meaning
Patient safety No avoidable harm
Effectiveness Evidence-based care
Patient-centredness Care that respects the patient
Timeliness Care without harmful delay
Efficiency No waste of time or supplies
Equity Same quality for the poor and the advantaged

Accreditation and standards

  • NABH — National Accreditation Board for hospitals
  • NQAS — National Quality Assurance Standards of India
  • Indian Healthcare Foundation (IHF) — India quality standards
  • Accreditation looks at clinical care, records, infection control, staff protection and integrity

Patient safety programmes

  • Medication safety: identify, read, dose, check, record
  • Fall prevention: bipedal risk assessment and bed rails
  • Infection control: hand hygiene, isolation, bundles
  • Safe surgery checklist
  • Bar-coding and feedback from incident reports

🔴 System problem, not blame

Most errors are system errors. Correct the system, the procedure or the design of the workflow rather than blaming one person. A strong safety culture makes staff report near misses.

🔴 Most important for exams

  1. Pillars of quality: safety, effectiveness, timeliness, equity, patient-centred.
  2. NABH and NQAS are the Indian quality standards.
  3. Audit compares practice against standards.
  4. Near-miss reporting is part of an effective safety workplace.
  5. Safe surgery checklist reduces operative errors.

⭐ Important for exams

  1. Falls, pressure ulcers and infections are nursing-sensitive indicators.
  2. Indicators and audit cycles drive improvement.
  3. Plan-Do-Check-Act is continuous improvement.
  4. Risk assessment and early warning systems save lives.
  5. Support and debriefing offset stress.

📌 Memory trick

Safety: F-M-A-S — Falls, Medication, Antimicrobial, Surgery checklist.

60-second revision

  • Quality pillars: safety, effectiveness, timeliness, efficiency, equity, patient-centredness.
  • Accreditation: NABH, NQAS, audits.
  • Safety programmes: medication, falls, infection, surgery checklists.
  • Blame-free, system corrective responses to incidents.
  • Care should be measured on outcomes and indicators.

Test yourself

The safe surgery checklist is used:

Answer: B. A safety checklist at three checkpoints in surgery prevents wrong-site and wrong-patient procedures.

NABH stands for:

Answer: A. The National Accreditation Board for Hospitals and Healthcare Providers sets hospital quality standards.

A fall prevention measure is:

Answer: B. Fall risk assessment on admission guides prevention such as rails, supervision and education.

A near miss is:

Answer: A. A near miss is an error that did not cause harm and must be reported for learning.

A blame-free culture in a unit:

Answer: B. Blame-free reporting encourages staff to report errors and near misses, which improves safety.
